children.text: arcitaḥ saṃsmṛto dhyātaḥ kīrtitaḥ kathitaḥ śrutaḥ
children.translated_text: May <s>Keśava</s>, who when worshipped, remembered, meditated upon, praised, spoken of, and heard of, indeed grants immortality, protect me.

children.text: yo dadāty amṛtatvaṃ hi sa māṃ rakṣatu keśavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He indeed grants immortality; may that <s>Keśava</s> protect me.

children.text: tāpatrayeṇa saṃtaptaṃ yad etad akhilaṃ jagat
children.translated_text: Since this whole world is scorched by the threefold suffering,
for its pacification I shall now teach the great ocean of the nectar of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.

children.text: te narāḥ paśavo loke kiṃ teṣāṃ jīvane phalam
children.translated_text: Those men in the world are beasts; what fruit is there in their life

children.text: yair na labdhā harer dīkṣā nārcito vā janārdanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: by whom initiation into <s>Hari</s> has not been obtained, or <s>Janārdana</s> has not been worshipped?
In this very terrible saṃsāra, troubled by birth, disease, and fear,

children.text: ayam eko mahābhāgaḥ pūjyate yad adhokṣajaḥ ||
children.translated_text: this alone is the great good fortune: that <s>Adhokṣaja</s> is worshipped.

children.text: sa nāma sukṛtī loke kulaṃ tena hy alaṃkṛtam
children.translated_text: He alone is called meritorious in the world, and by him his family is adorned,
by whom <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the support of all beings, has been pleased.

children.text: yajñānāṃ tapasāṃ caiva śubhānāṃ caiva karmaṇām
children.translated_text: Of sacrifices, austerities, and auspicious actions,
the constant worship of <s>Hari</s> is for men a fruit superior to these.
Those men who constantly worship <s>Hari</s> in the Kali age, the destroyer of Kali's impurity and remover of all sins,

children.text: ye 'rcayanti narā nityaṃ te 'pi vandyā yathā hariḥ ||
children.translated_text: they too are worthy of veneration, just like <s>Hari</s>.

children.text: nāsti śreyaskaraṃ nṛṇāṃ viṣṇor ārādhanān mune
children.translated_text: There is nothing more conducive to highest good for men than the worship of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, O sage;

children.text: yuge 'smiṃs tāmase loke satataṃ pūjyate nṛbhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: in this age, in this dark world, he is constantly worshipped by men.
When the lord of all gods, bearing conch, discus, and mace, has been worshipped,

children.text: arcitāḥ sarvadevāḥ syur yataḥ sarvagato hariḥ ||
children.translated_text: all the gods are worshipped, because <s>Hari</s> is present everywhere.
When <s>Keśava</s>, lord of all worlds, bowed to by gods and asuras,

children.text: keśave kaṃsakeśighne na yāti narakaṃ naraḥ ||
children.translated_text: the slayer of <s>Kaṃsa</s> and <s>Keśin</s>, has been duly worshipped, a man does not go to hell.
Having worshipped <s>Govinda</s> even once with a bilva leaf, a human being
becomes a sharer in liberation, free from distress, and dwells long in the world of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
By whom he has been worshipped even once, or bowed to even carelessly,

children.text: sa yāti paramaṃ sthānaṃ yat surair api durlabham ||
children.translated_text: that person goes to the supreme abode, which is difficult even for the gods to attain.
<s>Nārada</s>:
The worship of the lord of all worlds, the god of gods, the bearer of the Śārṅga bow,

children.text: sākṣād bhagavato viṣṇoḥ pūjanaṃ janmanaḥ phalam ||
children.translated_text: of the directly manifest blessed <s>Viṣṇu</s>, is the fruit of birth.
<s>Pulastya</s>:
When <s>Puruṣottama</s>, <s>Hari</s>, is worshipped by men with shoots of dūrvā grass and devotion,

children.text: harir dadāti hi phalaṃ sarvayajñaiś ca durlabham ||
children.translated_text: he gives a fruit difficult to obtain even by all sacrifices.
The god of gods, <s>Hari</s>, bearer of conch and discus, when worshipped according to rule,
gives an easily attainable fruit even when worshipped with water.
One being cooked in hell is rebuked by <s>Yama</s>:

children.text: kiṃ tvayā nārcito devaḥ keśavaḥ kleśanāśanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'Why was the god <s>Keśava</s>, destroyer of affliction, not worshipped by you?'
<s>Dharma</s>:
<s>Narasiṃha</s>, <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>, lotus-like in eye,

children.text: smaraṇān muktido nṛṇāṃ sa tvayā kiṃ na pūjitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: who grants liberation to men by remembrance, why was he not worshipped by you?

children.text: dravyāṇām apy abhāve tu salilenāpi pūjitaḥ
children.translated_text: Even when substances are lacking, if he is worshipped with water,

children.text: yo dadāti svakaṃ sthānaṃ sa tvayā kiṃ na pūjitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he gives his own abode; why was he not worshipped by you?
Those robbed and greatly corrupted are as though dead even while situated in the womb,

children.text: na prāptā yair harer dīkṣā sarvaduḥkhavimocanī ||
children.translated_text: by whom initiation into <s>Hari</s>, which releases from all suffering, has not been obtained.
<s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s>:
By whom <s>Janārdana</s>, the god of gods, has been worshipped even once,

children.text: yat kṛtaṃ tatkṛtaṃ tena samprāptaṃ paramaṃ padam ||
children.translated_text: by him what had to be done has been done, and the supreme state has been attained.
For dharma, wealth, desire, and liberation there is no other means
apart from the worship of <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>; I speak the truth, O lord of gods.
To that <s>Viṣṇu</s> of immeasurable splendor, the sacrifice-boar,

children.text: praṇāmaṃ ye 'pi kurvanti teṣām api namo namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: even those who make obeisance, to them too, repeated homage.
<s>Marīci</s>:
By men who have not worshipped <s>Govinda</s>, O son of a king,

children.text: na hi samprāpyate śreṣṭhaṃ tasmād ārādhayācyutam ||
children.translated_text: the highest abode is not attained; therefore worship <s>Acyuta</s>.
<s>Atri</s>:

children.text: paraḥ parāṇāṃ puruṣas tuṣṭo yasya janārdanaḥ
children.translated_text: The supreme person beyond the supreme is <s>Janārdana</s>; when he is pleased with someone,

children.text: sa cāpnoty akṣayaṃ sthānam etat satyaṃ mayoditam ||
children.translated_text: that person attains the imperishable abode. This has been truly spoken by me.
<s>Aṅgirāḥ</s>:
All this is within <s>Acyuta</s>, whose nature is renowned;

children.text: tam ārādhaya govindaṃ sthānam agryaṃ yadīcchasi ||
children.translated_text: worship that <s>Govinda</s>, if you desire the foremost abode.
<s>Pulaha</s>:

children.text: paraṃ brahma paraṃ dhāma yo 'sau brahma sanātanam
children.translated_text: He who is the supreme brahman, the supreme abode, that eternal brahman,

children.text: tam ārādhya hariṃ yāti muktim apy atidurlabhām ||
children.translated_text: having worshipped that <s>Hari</s>, one reaches liberation, though it is exceedingly hard to obtain.

children.text: aindram indraḥ paraṃ sthānaṃ yam ārādhya jagatpatim
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s> obtained the supreme station of Indra by worshipping the lord of the world,

children.text: prāpa yajñapatiṃ viṣṇuṃ tam ārādhaya suvrata ||
children.translated_text: <s>Viṣṇu</s>, lord of sacrifice; worship him, O you of good vow.

children.text: prāpnoty ārādhite viṣṇau manasā yad yad icchati
children.translated_text: When <s>Viṣṇu</s> is worshipped, one obtains whatever one desires in the mind,
whether a station contained within the three worlds, or still more one beyond the worlds.
Those who always remember <s>Viṣṇu</s>, bearer of conch, discus, and mace,
freed from all sin, enter the supreme brahman.

children.text: tato 'niruddhaṃ deveśaṃ pradyumnaṃ ca tataḥ param
children.translated_text: Then <s>Aniruddha</s>, lord of gods, and next <s>Pradyumna</s>,

children.text: tataḥ saṃkarṣaṇaṃ devaṃ vāsudevaṃ parāt param ||
children.translated_text: then the god <s>Saṃkarṣaṇa</s>, and <s>Vāsudeva</s>, higher than the highest.
There is nothing higher than <s>Vāsudeva</s>: this is the settled conclusion of the Vedānta.
For those who have entered <s>Vāsudeva</s>, how could there be return again?
<s>Ātreya</s>:

children.text: yo yān icchen naraḥ kāmān nārī vā varavarṇinī
children.translated_text: Whatever desires a man may wish for, or a woman of excellent complexion,
those abundant desires they obtain by fully worshipping <s>Janārdana</s>.
<s>Brahmā</s>:

children.text: bāhubhyāṃ sāgaraṃ tartuṃ ka iccheta pumān bhuvi
children.translated_text: What man on earth would wish to cross the ocean with his arms?

children.text: vāsudevam anārādhya ko mokṣaṃ gantum icchati ||
children.translated_text: Who would wish to go to liberation without worshipping <s>Vāsudeva</s>?
<s>Śaṃkara</s>:

children.text: kṛte pāpe 'nutāpo vai yasya puṃsaḥ prajāyate
children.translated_text: When remorse for sin arises in a man
the supreme expiation prescribed for him is remembrance of <s>Hari</s>.

children.text: na hy apuṇyavatāṃ loke mūḍhānāṃ kuṭilātmanām
children.translated_text: For devotion to <s>Govinda</s>, and likewise remembrance and praise, do not arise

children.text: bhaktir bhavati govinde smaraṇaṃ kīrtanaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: among the unmeritorious in the world, the deluded, and those of crooked nature.
At that very moment a person is freed from the suffering of birth, old age, and the rest,
self-controlled and purified in self, exactly when he remembers <s>Hari</s>.
When the terrible Kali age has arrived, devoid of dharma and knowledge,

children.text: na kaścit smarate devaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ kalimalāpaham ||
children.translated_text: no one remembers the god <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, remover of Kali's impurity.
In the Kali age, the foolish mortal does not perform remembrance and praise of <s>Hari</s>,

children.text: karoti martyo mūḍhātmā smaraṇaṃ kīrtanaṃ hareḥ ||
children.translated_text: the God of gods, who removes the suffering of birth.
Those who always remember <s>Viṣṇu</s> with a purified inner self

children.text: te prayānti bhavaṃ tyaktvā viṣṇulokam anāmayam ||
children.translated_text: go, after abandoning worldly existence, to the painless world of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
By the bonds of the world: womb, birth, old age, disease, and suffering,

children.text: na bādhyate naro nityaṃ vāsudevam anusmaran ||
children.translated_text: a man is never afflicted when he constantly remembers <s>Vāsudeva</s>.
The terribly dreadful path of <s>Yama</s>, the hells, and <s>Yama</s> himself,

children.text: svapne 'pi ca na paśyeta yaḥ smared garuḍadhvajam ||
children.translated_text: even in a dream he would not see, if he remembers the one whose banner bears <s>Garuḍa</s>.

children.text: hṛdi rūpaṃ mukhe nāma naivedyam udare hareḥ
children.translated_text: He in whose heart is the form, in whose mouth is the name, in whose belly is the food-offering of <s>Hari</s>,

children.text: pādodakaṃ ca nirmālyaṃ mastake yasya so 'cyutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and on whose head are the foot-water and the remains of worship: he is <s>Acyuta</s> himself.
Remembrance of <s>Govinda</s> burns up the great mountain-mass of men's sins
quickly and without doubt, as fire burns a heap of cotton.
<s>Agastya</s>:
By the mere remembrance of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the cage made of accumulated sins

children.text: śatadhā bhedam āyāti girir vajrahato yathā ||
children.translated_text: is shattered into a hundred pieces, as a mountain struck by a thunderbolt.

children.text: kṛṣṇe ratāḥ kṛṣṇam anusmarantaḥ tadbhāvitās tadgatamānasāś ca
children.translated_text: Those who are devoted to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, who remember <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, whose being is filled with him and whose minds have gone to him,

children.text: te bhinnadehāḥ praviśanti viṣṇuṃ havir yathā mantrahutaṃ hutāśe ||
children.translated_text: when separated from the body, enter <s>Viṣṇu</s>, as an oblation offered with mantras enters the sacrificial fire.

children.text: sā hānis tan mahat chidraṃ sā cāndhajaḍamūkatā
children.translated_text: That is loss, that is a great breach, and that is blindness, dullness, and muteness:

children.text: yan muhūrtaṃ kṣaṇaṃ vā 'pi vāsudevo na cintyate ||
children.translated_text: any moment or even instant in which <s>Vāsudeva</s> is not contemplated.

children.text: nārāyaṇo nāma naro narāṇāṃ prasaṃhya coraḥ kathitaḥ pṛthivyām
children.translated_text: The man named <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> is declared on earth to be a forceful thief among men,
for by being merely remembered he burns without remainder the accumulation of sins amassed over many births.
By the very remembrance of that <s>Vāsudeva</s>, wielder of the Śārṅga bow,
sin accumulated over ten million births perishes at that very instant.

children.text: kiṃ tasya bahubhis tīrthaiḥ kiṃ tapobhiḥ kim adhvaraiḥ
children.translated_text: What need has he of many sacred bathing-places, what of austerities, what of sacrifices,

children.text: yo nityaṃ dhyāyate devaṃ nārāyaṇam ananyadhīḥ ||
children.translated_text: who constantly meditates on the god <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> with undivided mind?

children.text: ye mānavā vigatarāgaparāvarajñā nārāyaṇaṃ suraguruṃ satataṃ smaranti
children.translated_text: Those humans, free from attachment and knowing higher and lower reality, who constantly remember <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the teacher of the gods,

children.text: dhyānena tena hatakilbiṣacetanāste mātuḥ payodhararasaṃ na punaḥ pibanti ||
children.translated_text: their minds cleansed of sin by that meditation, do not again drink the milk from a mother's breast.
O mind, here think on <s>Vāsudeva</s> day and night;

children.text: nūnaṃ yaś cintitaḥ puṃsāṃ hanti saṃsārabandhanam ||
children.translated_text: surely, when he is thought upon by men, he destroys the bondage of worldly existence.

children.text: āloḍya sarvaśāstrāṇi vicārya ca punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: Having churned all the scriptures and reflected again and again,

children.text: idam ekaṃ suniṣpannaṃ dhyeyo nārāyaṇaḥ sadā ||
children.translated_text: this one thing has been firmly established: <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> is always to be meditated upon.
When remembered, he becomes the vessel of every blessing;

children.text: puruṣas tam ajaṃ nityaṃ vrajāmi śaraṇaṃ harim ||
children.translated_text: I go for refuge to that unborn, eternal <s>Hari</s>, the supreme person.

children.text: vedeṣu yajñeṣu tapaḥsu caiva dāneṣu tīrtheṣu vrateṣu caiva
children.translated_text: Whatever merit is prescribed in the Vedas, in sacrifices, austerities, gifts, sacred fords, and vows,

children.text: iṣṭeṣu pūrteṣu ca yat pradiṣṭaṃ puṇyaṃ smṛte tat khalu vāsudeve ||
children.translated_text: and in rites for oneself and works for the public good, that indeed is obtained when <s>Vāsudeva</s> is remembered.
<s>Aurva</s>:

children.text: ārādhyaiva naro viṣṇuṃ manaso yad yad icchati
children.translated_text: Having worshipped <s>Viṣṇu</s>, a man obtains whatever his mind desires,

children.text: phalaṃ prāpnoty avikalaṃ bhūri svalpam athāpi vā ||
children.translated_text: the fruit entire, whether great or small.
The singing of his name with devotion is the unsurpassed dissolver,
O <s>Maitreya</s>, of all sins, just as fire is of metals.
The exceedingly fierce impurity of the Kali age, which gives men the torment of hell,
at once goes to dissolution when <s>Acyuta</s> is praised even once.
Those who take refuge in <s>Keśava</s> attain liberation without difficulty;
to obstruct that, adversaries such as <s>Śakra</s> arise.
Having reached the four oceans in the excellent <s>Jambūdvīpa</s>, somewhere,
there is no healer of all sins for a man other than <s>Keśava</s>.

children.text: yad abhyarcya hariṃ bhaktyā kṛte varṣaśatair api
children.translated_text: The fruit that one obtains entire in the Kṛta age by worshipping <s>Hari</s> with devotion for hundreds of years,

children.text: phalaṃ prāpnoty avikalaṃ kalau saṃkīrtya keśavam ||
children.translated_text: one obtains in the Kali age by praising <s>Keśava</s>.

children.text: kṣīyate tu yadā dharmaḥ prāpte ghore kalau yuge
children.translated_text: But when <s>dharma</s> declines, when the dreadful Kali age has arrived,

children.text: tadā na kīrtayet kaścin muktidaṃ devam acyutam ||
children.translated_text: then hardly anyone praises the liberating god <s>Acyuta</s>.
When his name is uttered even involuntarily, from all sins
a man is immediately released, as deer flee from a lion in terror.
There is the mantra '<s>Nārāyaṇa</s>,' and speech is under one's control;

children.text: tathā 'pi narake ghore majjantīty etad adbhutam ||
children.translated_text: yet people sink in dreadful hell. This is astonishing.

children.text: ārtā viṣaṇṇāḥ śithilāś ca bhītā ghoreṣu ca vyādhiṣu vartamānāḥ
children.translated_text: The afflicted, despondent, weakened, and frightened, while abiding in terrible diseases,
by merely uttering the word <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, become freed from suffering and happy.
<s>Kauśika</s>:

children.text: sakṛd uccāritaṃ yais tu kṛṣṇeti na viśanti te
children.translated_text: Those by whom '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>' has been uttered even once do not enter

children.text: garbhāgāraṃ gṛhaṃ mātur yamalokaṃ ca dussaham ||
children.translated_text: the chamber of the womb, the house of the mother, nor the unbearable world of <s>Yama</s>.
How far apart is going to the surface of heaven, marked by return,
and how far apart is the recitation '<s>Vāsudeva</s>,' the unsurpassed seed of liberation!

children.text: buddhyā buddhvā vadasvainaṃ harir ity akṣaradvayam
children.translated_text: Understanding it with your intellect, utter these two syllables: '<s>Hari</s>';

children.text: smaraṇād eva kṛṣṇasya na punarjāyate kvacit ||
children.translated_text: by the mere remembrance of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, one is never born again anywhere.

children.text: he jihve mama niḥsnehe hariṃ kiṃ nuna bhāṣase
children.translated_text: O my tongue, loveless as you are, why do you not speak of <s>Hari</s>?
Speak '<s>Hari</s>,' O auspicious one; <s>Hari</s> is the boat across the ocean of worldly existence.

children.text: asāre khalu saṃsāre sārāt sārataro hariḥ
children.translated_text: In this worthless worldly existence, <s>Hari</s> is the essence more essential than essence itself;

children.text: puṇyahīnā na vindanti sāraṅgāś ca yathā jalam ||
children.translated_text: those lacking merit do not find him, just as thirsty creatures do not find water.

children.text: kurukṣetreṇa kiṃ tasya kiṃ kāśyā puṣkareṇa vā
children.translated_text: What need has he of <s>Kurukṣetra</s>, or of <s>Kāśī</s> or <s>Puṣkara</s>,

children.text: jihvāgre vartate tasya harir ity akṣaradvayam ||
children.translated_text: on the tip of whose tongue are the two syllables '<s>Hari</s>'?
<s>Brahmā</s> said:

children.text: asāre khalu saṃsāre sāram ekaṃ nirūpitam
children.translated_text: In this worthless worldly existence, one essence has been determined:
the essence is the worship of <s>Hari</s>, lord of all worlds.

children.text: sā jihvā yā hariṃ stauti tac cittaṃ yat tadarpaṇam
children.translated_text: That is a tongue which praises <s>Hari</s>; that is a mind which is offered to him;

children.text: tāv eva kevalau ślāghyau yau tatpūjākarau karau ||
children.translated_text: only those two hands are praiseworthy which perform his worship.

children.text: yas tu viṣṇuparo nityaṃ dṛḍhabhaktir jitendriyaḥ
children.translated_text: But he who is always devoted to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, firm in devotion, and master of his senses...

children.text: svagṛhe 'pi vasan yāti tad viṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam ||
children.translated_text: Even while living in his own house, he goes to that supreme abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
<s>Śaṅkara</s>:
Well done, well done, greatly fortunate one; well done, destroyer of demons.

children.text: yan māṃ pṛcchasi dharmajña keśavārādhanaṃ prati ||
children.translated_text: Since, knower of <s>dharma</s>, you ask me about the worship of <s>Keśava</s>,

children.text: nimiṣaṃ nimiṣārdhaṃ vā muhūrtam api bhārgava
children.translated_text: for a moment, or half a moment, or even for a muhūrta, O descendant of <s>Bhṛgu</s>,
devotion to <s>Keśava</s> does not arise in those whose entire mass of sins has not been burned away.

children.text: kiṃ tena manasā kāryaṃ yan na tiṣṭhati keśave
children.translated_text: What use is that mind which does not rest in <s>Keśava</s>?
The mind is the effective cause for attaining the fruit of liberation.

children.text: rogo nāma na sā jihvā yayā na stūyate hariḥ
children.translated_text: That is no tongue, but rather a disease, by which <s>Hari</s> is not praised.

children.text: gartau nāma na tau karṇau yābhyāṃ tat karma na śrutam ||
children.translated_text: Those are no ears, but rather pits, by which his deeds have not been heard.
Surely that is a swelling in the throat, or else merely a little appendage of the tongue.

children.text: rogo nāma na sā jihvā yā na vakti harer guṇān ||
children.translated_text: That is no tongue, but a disease, which does not speak of the virtues of <s>Hari</s>.

children.text: bhārabhūtaiḥ kāryam ebhiḥ kiṃ tasya nṛpaśor dvija
children.translated_text: What is the use, O twice-born, of these burdensome limbs belonging to that man-beast?
Those two feet are fruitful which go to the temple of <s>Keśava</s>,

children.text: te ca netre mahābhāga yābhyāṃ saṃdṛśyate hariḥ ||
children.translated_text: and those eyes, greatly fortunate one, by which <s>Hari</s> is beheld.

children.text: kiṃ tasya caraṇaiḥ kāryaṃ vṛthāsañcaraṇair dvija
children.translated_text: What use are his feet, O twice-born, wandering about in vain,

children.text: yair hi na vrajate jantuḥ keśavālayadarśane ||
children.translated_text: with which a creature does not go to see the temple of <s>Keśava</s>?
Even the seerhood of sages who know the Veda and Vedāṅgas, whose selves are purified,
should be understood, knower of <s>dharma</s>, to arise from his grace.
Those who enjoy great pleasures on couches of varied jewels
and sport with heavenly women do so as the fruit of remembering <s>Keśava</s>.
If someone were to perform a thousand sets of a thousand horse-sacrifices,

children.text: nāsau tat phalam āpnoti tadbhaktair yad avāpyate ||
children.translated_text: he would not obtain the fruit that is obtained by devotees of him.

children.text: re re manuṣyāḥ puruṣottamasya karau na kasmān mukulīkurudhve
children.translated_text: O men, why do you not fold your hands to <s>Puruṣottama</s>?

children.text: kriyājuṣāṃ ko bhavatāṃ prayāsaḥ phalaṃ hi yat padam acyutasya ||
children.translated_text: What exertion is there for you who are devoted to rites, when the fruit is indeed the foot of <s>Acyuta</s>?

children.text: viṣṇor vimānaṃ yaḥ kuryāt sakṛd bhaktyā pradakṣiṇam
children.translated_text: A man who once, with devotion, circumambulates the shrine of <s>Viṣṇu</s>
obtains the fruit of a thousand horse-sacrifices.
But one who performs circumambulation endowed with devotion to <s>Hari</s>
goes to the world of <s>Viṣṇu</s> in an aerial car yoked with swans.
Millions of thousands of sacred fords and hundreds of millions of vows
are not worth even a sixteenth part of a prostration to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.

children.text: urasā śirasā dṛṣṭyā manasā vacasā tathā
children.translated_text: With the chest, the head, the sight, the mind, and likewise with speech,
with the feet, the hands, and the knees, prostration is declared to be eight-limbed.
For one who makes obeisance to the wielder of <s>Śārṅga</s>, even deceitfully,

children.text: śātajanmārjitaṃ pāpaṃ naśyaty eva na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: sin accumulated over a hundred births is certainly destroyed; there is no doubt.
For men of sinful deeds who are sunk in the ocean of saṃsāra,

children.text: nānyo dhartā jagannāthaṃ muktvā nārāyaṇaṃ param ||
children.translated_text: there is no other supporter besides <s>Jagannātha</s>, the supreme <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.
As many particles as there are on the body of one whose limbs are covered with dust, O <s>Bhārata</s>,
for that many thousands of years he is honored in the world of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
The purifying food offered to <s>Viṣṇu</s> is remembered by the sages as excellent food.
Having eaten food offered to another deity, one should perform the cāndrāyaṇa penance.
The fruit that is obtained by men through thousands of crores of lunar vows and crores of month-long fasts

children.text: yat phalaṃ labhyate puṃbhir viṣṇor naivedyabhakṣaṇāt ||
children.translated_text: is obtained from eating the food offered to <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
Whatever rivers do not reach the ocean grant the fruit of a three-night observance.

children.text: samudragās tu pakṣasya māsasya saritāṃ patiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those that reach the ocean grant the fruit of a fortnight; the lord of rivers grants that of a month.
The <s>Godā</s> grants the fruit of six months, and the <s>Jāhnavī</s> that of a year.
These are not worth even a sixteenth part of the water from <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s feet.
<s>Gaṅgā</s>, <s>Prayāga</s>, <s>Gayā</s>, <s>Puṣkara</s>, <s>Naimiṣa</s>, and the regions of <s>Kurujāṅgala</s>, though visited many times,

children.text: kālena tīrthasalilāni punanti pāpaṃ pādodakaṃ bhagavataḥ prapunāti sadyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the waters of sacred fords purify sin over time, but the foot-water of the Lord purifies at once.

children.text: yāni kāni ca tīrthāni brahmāṇḍāntargatāni vai
children.translated_text: Whatever sacred fords there are within the cosmic egg,
these are not worth even a sixteenth part of the water from <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s feet.

children.text: snānaṃ pādodakaṃ viṣṇoḥ piban śirasi dhārayan
children.translated_text: Bathing in, drinking, and placing on the head the water from <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s feet,
one becomes freed from all sins and attains Vaiṣṇava perfection.
Just as the foot-water is holy, so too are the offered garland, the unguent,

children.text: naivedyaṃ dhūpaśeṣaṃ ca ārārttiś ca tathā hareḥ ||
children.translated_text: the food-offering, the remnant of incense, and likewise the ārati of <s>Hari</s>.

children.text: tulasyās tu rajojuṣṭaṃ naivedyasya ca bhakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Eating the offering mixed with the dust of <s>Tulasī</s>,
and bearing the offered garland on the head, destroys even great sins.

children.text: bhaktyā vā yadi vābhaktyā cakrāṅkitaśilām prati
children.translated_text: Whether with devotion or without devotion, toward the stone marked with the discus,
seeing it or even touching it destroys all sins.
The deity born from <s>Śālagrāma</s> and the deity arising from <s>Dvāravatī</s>,
by the bathing water of both, one removes the sin of killing a brāhmaṇa.
In a land of mlecchas or even in an impure place, wherever the discus-marked one stands,

children.text: yojanāni tathā trīṇi mama kṣetraṃ vasundhare ||
children.translated_text: for three yojanas around, O <s>Vasundharā</s>, that is my sacred field.
Wherever the deity born from <s>Śālagrāma</s>, the stone adorned with the mark of the discus,
is carried, there is more than a hundredfold <s>Vārāṇasī</s>.
The deity born from <s>Śālagrāma</s> and the deity arising from <s>Dvāravatī</s>,

children.text: ubhayoḥ saṃgamo yatra tatra muktir na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: where the conjunction of the two occurs, there is liberation; there is no doubt.
Since liberation is given here by <s>Hari</s>, all places of liberation exist everywhere.

children.text: sa yasya sarvabhāveṣu tasya taiḥ kiṃ prayojanam ||
children.translated_text: For one for whom he is present in all states of being, what need has that person of those places?

children.text: harir yāti harir yāti dasyuvyājena yo vadet
children.translated_text: If someone says, 'Hari goes, Hari goes,' even under the pretext of a robber,

children.text: so 'pi sadgatim āpnoti gatiṃ sukṛtino yathā ||
children.translated_text: he too obtains a good destination, like the destination of the meritorious.
Those who abandon <s>Vāsudeva</s> and worship another deity,

children.text: tyaktvā 'mṛtaṃ sa mūḍhātmā bhuṅkte hālāhalaṃ viṣam ||
children.translated_text: that deluded self, having abandoned nectar, consumes the hālāhala poison.

children.text: tyaktvāmṛtaṃ yathā kaścid anyapānaṃ piben naraḥ
children.translated_text: Just as a man might abandon nectar and drink some other beverage,

children.text: tathā hariṃ parityajya cānyaṃ devam upāsate ||
children.translated_text: so do they abandon <s>Hari</s> and worship another deity.

children.text: svadharmaṃ tu parityajya paradharmaṃ yathā caret
children.translated_text: But just as one might abandon one’s own <s>dharma</s> and practice another’s <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: tathā hariṃ parityajya cānyaṃ devam upāsate ||
children.translated_text: so they abandon <s>Hari</s> and worship another deity.

children.text: gāṃ ca tyaktvā vimūḍhātmā gardabhīṃ vandate yathā
children.translated_text: Just as a deluded man, abandoning a cow, bows to a she-ass,

children.text: tathā hariṃ parityajya cānyaṃ devam upāsate ||
children.translated_text: so they abandon <s>Hari</s> and worship another deity.
He who abandons <s>Vāsudeva</s> and worships another deity
is a fool who, thirsty on the bank of the <s>Jāhnavī</s>, digs a well.

children.text: yathā gaṅgodakaṃ tyaktvā pibet kūpodakaṃ naraḥ
children.translated_text: Just as a man might abandon the water of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> and drink well-water,

children.text: tathā hariṃ parityajya yo 'nyaṃ devam upāsate ||
children.translated_text: so does one who abandons <s>Hari</s> and worships another deity.
He is like one who abandons his own mother and bows instead to an outcaste woman;

children.text: tathā hariṃ parityajya yo 'nyaṃ devam upāsate ||
children.translated_text: so does one who abandons <s>Hari</s> and worships another deity.

children.text: yāvat svastham idaṃ piṇḍaṃ nirujaṃ karaṇānvitam
children.translated_text: As long as this bodily mass is healthy, free from disease, and endowed with the faculties,
so long perform what is beneficial for yourself; afterward you will be tormented by regret.

children.text: yāvat svāsthyaṃ śarīreṣu karaṇeṣu ca pāṭavam
children.translated_text: As long as there is health in the body and skill in the faculties,

children.text: tāvad arcaya govindam āyuṣyaṃ sārthakaṃ kuru ||
children.translated_text: so long worship <s>Govinda</s>; make your lifespan meaningful.

children.text: smaryatāṃ tu hṛṣīkeśo hṛṣīkeṣu dṛḍheṣu ca
children.translated_text: Let <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s> be remembered while the senses are still firm;
when the senses are no longer firm, who remembers <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>?
As long as a creature thinks about sense-objects, which are like poison,

children.text: tāvac cet smarate viṣṇuṃ ko na mucyeta bandhanāt ||
children.translated_text: if for that long he remembers <s>Viṣṇu</s>, who would not be released from bondage?
As long as a creature talks about sense-objects, which are like poison,

children.text: tāvac cet smarate viṣṇuṃ ko na mucyeta bandhanāt ||
children.translated_text: if for that long he remembers <s>Viṣṇu</s>, who would not be released from bondage?
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: jñātvā viprās tithiṃ samyag daivajñaiḥ samudīritām
children.translated_text: Having correctly learned the lunar date, O brāhmaṇas, as declared by astrologers,

children.text: kartavya upavāsaś ca anyathā narakaṃ vrajet ||
children.translated_text: one should perform the fast; otherwise one would go to hell.

children.text: kṣaye vāpy athavā vṛddhau samprāpte vā dinakṣaye
children.translated_text: Whether there is loss or increase of a lunar date, or when the lunar date ends during the day,
the holy <s>Dvādaśī</s> should be fasted on, and one should abandon an <s>Ekādaśī</s> touched by the preceding date.
A man who observes one touched by the preceding date cuts away his <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: saṃtates tu vināśāya sampado haraṇāya ca ||
children.translated_text: and it leads to the destruction of offspring and to the loss of wealth.
When even a small portion touches it, O best of brāhmaṇas, one should reject an <s>Ekādaśī</s> joined with <s>Daśamī</s>,

children.text: surāyā bindunā spṛṣṭaṃ gaṅgāmbha iva saṃtyajet ||
children.translated_text: as one rejects <s>Gaṅgā</s> water touched by a drop of liquor.

children.text: śvadṛtau pañcagavyaṃ ca daśamyā dūṣitāṃ tyajet
children.translated_text: One should reject <s>Ekādaśī</s> spoiled by <s>Daśamī</s>, O best twice-born,
in both fortnights, just as one rejects pañcagavya in a dog-skin vessel.

children.text: tasmād viprā na viddhā hi kartavyaikādaśī kvacit
children.translated_text: Therefore, O brāhmaṇas, an <s>Ekādaśī</s> that is tainted should never be observed.

children.text: viddhā hanti purāpuṇyaṃ śrāddhaṃ ca vṛṣalīpatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: A tainted one destroys former merit, just as a śrāddha performed by the husband of a śūdra woman does.

children.text: japtaṃ dattaṃ hutaṃ snātaṃ tathā pūjā kṛtā hareḥ
children.translated_text: What is recited, given, offered in the fire, bathed for, and likewise the worship performed for <s>Hari</s>,

children.text: tat sarvaṃ vilayaṃ yāti tamaḥ sūryodaye yathā ||
children.translated_text: all that comes to dissolution, as darkness at sunrise.
When, O brāhman, on <s>Ekādaśī</s> there is a lunar date ending during the day,

children.text: upoṣyā dvādaśī tatra trayodaśyāṃ tu pāraṇam ||
children.translated_text: then <s>Dvādaśī</s> should be fasted on, and the breaking of the fast is on <s>Trayodaśī</s>.
All lunar dates beginning with <s>Pratipad</s> are to be known as complete
from sunrise to sunrise, except for <s>Harivāsara</s>.
But if <s>Daśamī</s> is seen at the time of dawn’s redness,
then fasting on <s>Ekādaśī</s> should be known as rooted in sin.
But if <s>Daśamī</s> is seen at the time of dawn’s redness,
<s>Ekādaśī</s> is not to be observed there, for it destroys <s>dharma</s>, desire, and wealth.
Four ghaṭikās in the morning are called aruṇodaya, the red dawn;
this is remembered as the bathing time of ascetics, equal to the water of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>.
When, O brāhmaṇas, before sunrise it is accompanied by two muhūrtas,
that is called a complete <s>Ekādaśī</s>; the observer of the vow should fast only then.

children.text: udayāt prāk trighaṭikā vyāpiny ekādaśī yadā
children.translated_text: When <s>Ekādaśī</s> extends for three ghaṭikās before sunrise,
it is called a doubtful <s>Ekādaśī</s> and should be avoided, for it destroys <s>dharma</s> and wealth.
For the increase of sons and grandsons one should have the fast performed on <s>Dvādaśī</s>.

children.text: tatra kratuśataṃ puṇyaṃ trayodaśyāṃ tu pāraṇaṃ ||
children.translated_text: There the merit is that of a hundred sacrifices, and the fast is to be broken on <s>Trayodaśī</s>.
When <s>Ekādaśī</s> extends for two ghaṭikās before sunrise,
it is called a mixed <s>Ekādaśī</s> and should be avoided by those who desire <s>dharma</s> and wealth.
For the increase of sons and kingdom, fasting should be on <s>Dvādaśī</s>.

children.text: tatra kratuśataṃ puṇyaṃ trayodaśyāṃ tu pāraṇam ||
children.translated_text: There the merit is that of a hundred sacrifices, and the fast is to be broken on <s>Trayodaśī</s>.
The one joined with the remainder of <s>Daśamī</s> was fasted on by <s>Gāndhārī</s>;

children.text: tasyāḥ putraśataṃ naṣṭaṃ tasmāt tāṃ parivarjayet ||
children.translated_text: her hundred sons were destroyed, therefore one should completely avoid that one.
When there are conflicts among many scriptures and disputes among brāhmaṇas,

children.text: upoṣyā dvādaśī puṇyā trayodaśyāṃ tu pāraṇam ||
children.translated_text: the holy <s>Dvādaśī</s> should be fasted on, and the fast should be broken on <s>Trayodaśī</s>.

children.text: ekādaśyāṃ tu viddhāyāṃ samprāpte śravaṇe tathā
children.translated_text: When <s>Ekādaśī</s> is tainted, and likewise when <s>Śravaṇa</s> has arrived,

children.text: upoṣyā dvādaśī puṇyā pakṣayor ubhayor api ||
children.translated_text: the holy <s>Dvādaśī</s> should be fasted on in both fortnights.
Thousands of eclipses, tens of thousands of vyatīpātas,

children.text: amālakṣaṃ tu dvādaśyāḥ kalāṃ nārhanti ṣoḍaśīm ||
children.translated_text: and a hundred thousand new-moon days are not worth a sixteenth part of <s>Dvādaśī</s>.

children.text: śuddhāpi dvādaśī grāhyā parato dvādaśī yadi
children.translated_text: Even a pure <s>Dvādaśī</s> is to be accepted if there is another <s>Dvādaśī</s> afterward.

children.text: viṣaṃ tu daśamī jñeyā 'mṛtaṃ caikādaśī tithiḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Daśamī</s> should be known as poison, and the <s>Ekādaśī</s> lunar date as nectar;
one in which poison predominates should be avoided, but one with nectar should chiefly be accepted.
Eating on <s>Dvādaśī</s> and fasting for <s>Hari</s> on a tainted day,
whoever does this out of dull-mindedness reaches hell.

children.text: yāni kāni ca vākyāni viddhopāsyāparāṇi tu
children.translated_text: Whatever statements there are that favor worship on a tainted day
are devoted to the worship of <s>Dhanada</s>; they are not Vaiṣṇava even in ten thousand cases.
Or else, for the sake of delusion, by <s>Mohinī</s>, the blessed <s>Hari</s>,
<s>Janārdana</s> in the form of <s>Vyāsa</s>, being entreated, caused them to be made.
For the increase of the worship of <s>Dhanada</s> and of a great treasury,
for the delusion of the asuras and for the increase of heretics,
and so that they might not know their own true nature and might not attain that true nature.
Thus, by abandoning the tainted one and fasting on <s>Dvādaśī</s>,
sin accumulated over ten million births is destroyed by that one observance alone,
and even sin ten million times greater than that, forbidden for other people, is destroyed.

children.text: yad anādikṛtaṃ pāpaṃ tad ūrdhvaṃ yat kariṣyati
children.translated_text: Whatever sin has been committed from beginningless time, and whatever one will commit thereafter,

children.text: tat sarvaṃ vilayaṃ yāti pareṣām upavāsanāt
children.translated_text: all that goes to dissolution through fasting on these superior days.

children.text: na ca tasmāt priyatamaḥ keśavasya mamāpi vā ||
children.translated_text: And there is no one dearer than him to <s>Keśava</s>, or even to me.

children.text: ekādaśyā hy avedhe tu dvādaśīṃ na parityajet
children.translated_text: When Ekādaśī is not pierced, one should not abandon Dvādaśī.

children.text: pāraṇe maraṇe caiva tithis tātkālikī smṛtā ||
children.translated_text: For breaking a fast and for death, the tithi current at that time is remembered as authoritative.

children.text: brahmacārī gṛhastho vā vānaprastho yatis tathā
children.translated_text: Whether a celibate student, a householder, a forest-dweller, or an ascetic,

children.text: brāhmaṇaḥ kṣatriyo vaiśyaḥ śūdro bhartṛmatī tathā ||
children.translated_text: whether a brāhmaṇa, kṣatriya, vaiśya, śūdra, or a woman with a husband,
or one without a husband, or others such as sūtas and vaidehikas,

children.text: ekādaśyāṃ na bhuñjīta pakṣayor ubhayor api ||
children.translated_text: one should not eat on Ekādaśī in either of the two fortnights.
But the person who eats on Ekādaśī, whose mind is covered by delusion,

children.text: śuklāyām atha kṛṣṇāyāṃ nirayaṃ yāti sa dhruvam ||
children.translated_text: whether on the bright or on the dark one, certainly goes to hell.
The sinner who, out of delusion, makes a distinction, saying 'bright' and 'dark,'

children.text: ekādaśīṃ sa vai yāti nirayaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: indeed goes to hell with respect to Ekādaśī; there is no doubt here.

children.text: yathā gaur naiva hantavyā śuklā kṛṣṇeti bhāmini
children.translated_text: Just as a cow is not to be killed by distinguishing 'white' or 'black,' O fair lady,

children.text: ekādaśyāṃ na bhuñjīta pakṣayor ubhayor api ||
children.translated_text: one should not eat on Ekādaśī in either of the two fortnights.
Whatever statements there are about excluding the dark Ekādaśī,
even where there is prohibition in connection with <s>Bharaṇī</s> and the like, those apply to people seeking optional desired fruits.
Even those who have desires should perform fasting for the sake of the obligatory purpose,

children.text: prīṇanārthaṃ harer nityaṃ na tu kāmavyapekṣayā ||
children.translated_text: always for the pleasing of <s>Hari</s>, and not with dependence on desire.
Therefore, whether bright or dark, even when joined with <s>Bharaṇī</s> and the like,
one should always fast in order to avoid transgression,
or for the pleasing of <s>Hari</s> and for the attainment of the world of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: kalā vā ghaṭikā vāpi apare dvādaśī yadi
children.translated_text: If, on the following day, there is Dvādaśī even for a kalā or a ghaṭikā,
one destroys twelve Dvādaśīs by breaking the fast on the previous day.

children.text: atiriktā dvādaśī cet sa tāṃ nopoṣayed yadi
children.translated_text: If Dvādaśī is extended and one does not fast on it,
one destroys twelve Dvādaśīs, and Dvādaśī itself has been overstepped.
When Dvādaśī is extended, the person who eats on the previous day
destroys twelve Dvādaśīs; one should not abandon Dvādaśī.
The very dull-witted person who does not fast on a Dvādaśī joined with <s>Śravaṇa</s>
has the merit he has produced over five years perish.
Having fasted on Ekādaśī, one should then fast on Dvādaśī as well.

children.text: na tatra vidhilopaḥ syād ubhayor devatā hariḥ ||
children.translated_text: There is no failure of rule there, since <s>Hari</s> is the deity of both.
Having broken the fast even with water, one who eats is not at fault.
For water has been declared by the learned to be both eaten and not eaten.
And so, with water alone, I shall perform the breaking of the vow.

children.text: na kāśī na gayā gaṅgā na revā na ca gautamī
children.translated_text: Neither <s>Kāśī</s>, nor <s>Gayā</s>, nor <s>Gaṅgā</s>, nor <s>Revā</s>, nor <s>Gautamī</s>,

children.text: na cāpi kauravaṃ kṣetraṃ samā bhūpa harer dināt ||
children.translated_text: nor even the field of the <s>Kauravas</s>, O king, is equal to the day of <s>Hari</s>.
Thousands of horse-sacrifices and tens of thousands of Vājapeya sacrifices
are not worth even a sixteenth part of fasting on Ekādaśī.
By the fire arising from Ekādaśī, the fuel of sin
is reduced to ashes, O king of kings, even if it has arisen over a hundred births.

children.text: nedṛśaṃ pāvanaṃ kiṃcin narāṇāṃ bhuvi vidyate
children.translated_text: There is nothing on earth so purifying for human beings
as the day of <s>Padmanābha</s>, which removes sin.
So long do sins remain in this body, O lord of men,
as a creature does not fast on the auspicious day of <s>Padmanābha</s>.

children.text: ekādaśendriyaiḥ pāpaṃ yat kṛtaṃ bhavati prabho
children.translated_text: Whatever sin has been committed by the eleven senses, O lord,
by fasting on Ekādaśī one should bring all that to dissolution.
There is nothing equal to Ekādaśī as protection from sin.

children.text: vyājenāpi kṛtā rājan na darśayati bhāskarim ||
children.translated_text: Even when performed by pretext, O king, it does not show one the sun.
Blessed <s>Vedavyāsa</s> said:

children.text: sa brahmahā sa goghnaś ca stenaḥ sa gurutalpagaḥ
children.translated_text: He is a killer of a brāhmaṇa, he is a cow-killer, he is a thief, and he violates his guru's bed,

children.text: ekādaśyāṃ tu bhuñjānaḥ pakṣayor ubhayor api ||
children.translated_text: if he eats on Ekādaśī in either of the two fortnights.
Better intercourse with one's own mother, better the eating of cow's flesh,

children.text: varaṃ hatyā surāpānam ekādaśyāṃ tu bhojanāt ||
children.translated_text: better killing and drinking liquor than eating on Ekādaśī.
Those lowest men who eat on the holy day of Ekādaśī,
after looking at their face, one should look at the sun.
All the sins on earth, beginning with the killing of a brāhmaṇa,
take refuge in food when the day of <s>Hari</s> has arrived.
<s>Rugmāṅgada</s>:

children.text: aṣṭavarṣādhiko yas tu aśītir na hi pūryate
children.translated_text: Whoever is older than eight years and has not completed eighty,

children.text: yo bhuṅkte mānavaḥ pāpo viṣṇor ahani cāgate ||
children.translated_text: that sinful human being who eats when the day of <s>Viṣṇu</s> has arrived,

children.text: pitā vā yadi vā putro bhāryā vā 'pi suhṛjjanaḥ
children.translated_text: whether father, son, wife, or even a friend,
if he eats on the day of <s>Padmanābha</s>, he should be restrained like a robber.
<s>Dharmavibhūṣaṇa</s>:
In the morning, on the day of <s>Hari</s>, people, remain taking only one meal,
all without alkali and salt, eating sacrificially pure food.
Sleeping on the ground, free from union with your beloveds,
remember the lord of the gods, the ancient supreme person.
Though connected with a single meal, you will be in a state of fasting,
with accumulations of śrāddhas not performed, and with rites of water and water-balls.
<s>Brahmā</s>:
Having fasted on the holy Dvādaśī, which grants the destruction of all sins,

children.text: na paśyati yamaṃ vā 'pi narakān na ca yātanām ||
children.translated_text: one does not see <s>Yama</s>, nor hells, nor torment.
The Purāṇas proclaim here again and again, O lovely-faced one:

children.text: na bhoktavyaṃ na bhoktavyaṃ samprāpte harivāsare ||
children.translated_text: One must not eat, one must not eat, when the day of <s>Hari</s> has arrived.

children.text: dvādaśī na pramoktavyā yāvad āyuḥ pravartate
children.translated_text: Dvādaśī is not to be neglected as long as life goes on.
<s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s> should be worshiped with a purified inner self.

children.text: bhaktyā grāhyo hṛṣīkeśo na dhanair dharaṇīsurāḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s> is to be grasped by devotion, not by wealth, O brāhmaṇas.

children.text: bhaktyā sampūjito viṣṇuḥ phalaṃ datte samīhitam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Viṣṇu</s>, worshiped with devotion, gives the desired fruit.
Even when worshiped with water, <s>Jagannātha</s>, the destroyer of affliction,

children.text: paritoṣaṃ prayāty āśu tṛṣārtās tu yathā jalaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: quickly becomes satisfied, just as the thirsty are satisfied with waters.
Whether I am sitting, lying down, standing, or even walking,
delight always in my heart, O lotus-eyed one.
And since you are all-pervading, the self of all, O <s>Acyuta</s>, in all states,
delight in my heart, O lotus-eyed <s>Nṛsiṃha</s>.
Give me a handhold, O blessed <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, lotus-eyed one,
as I am always sinking in the terrible muddy ocean of becoming.
Protect me, protect me, O lord of the world, <s>Vāsudeva</s>, <s>Acyuta</s>, imperishable one.
Lift me up, O <s>Govinda</s>, from the ocean of painful saṃsāra.

children.text: etat puṇyaṃ paraṃ guhyaṃ pavitraṃ pāpanāśanam
children.translated_text: This meritorious teaching is supreme, secret, purifying, and destructive of sin;
it grants long life and fame, and destroys the evil dreams of the Kali age.
In the Kali age, whatever measure of sin arises from killing, theft, and the like,
when <s>Govinda</s> is remembered in the mind, it is burned like a heap of cotton.

children.text: kalau keśavabhaktānāṃ na bhayaṃ vidyate kvacit
children.translated_text: In the Kali age there is never any fear anywhere for the devotees of <s>Keśava</s>.

children.text: smṛte saṃkīrtite dhyāte saṃkṣayaṃ yāti pātakam ||
children.translated_text: When he is remembered, praised aloud, and meditated upon, sin goes to destruction.
This śāstra should be studied; it should be heard without envy.

children.text: bhaktebhyaś ca pradātavyaṃ dhārmikebhyaḥ punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And it should be given again and again to devotees and to righteous people.

children.text: adhīyāna idaṃ śāstram viṣṇor māhātmyam uttamam
children.translated_text: One who studies this śāstra, the highest greatness of <s>Viṣṇu</s>,
becomes freed from all sins and attains the supreme state.

children.text: śrutvā dharmaṃ vijānāti śrutvā tyajati durmatim
children.translated_text: By hearing, one understands dharma; by hearing, one abandons wrong understanding.

children.text: śrutvā jñānam avāpnoti śrutvā mokṣaṃ ca gacchati ||
children.translated_text: By hearing, one obtains knowledge; by hearing, one goes to liberation.

children.text: tasmād idaṃ samāśrāvyaṃ śrotavyaṃ ca sadaiva hi
children.translated_text: Therefore this should be made to be heard, and should always indeed be heard.
But it must never be given in any way to those burned by the forest fire of bad reasoning.
For creatures on earth who have died from drinking the poison of saṃsāra,
the <s>Kṛṣṇāmṛtamahārṇava</s>, remembered for them, is for immortality.
The one whose body is always moistened with the water from his feet
becomes, every day, as one bathed in thousands of crores of tīrthas.
What use is there in thousands of crores of tīrthas being visited,
if one regularly drinks the water fallen from the sālagrāma stone?
Those who day after day make contact with the sālagrāma stone,
the gods, together with <s>Vāsava</s>, desire the touch of their hands.
The fire of hell is unbearable; the servants of <s>Yama</s> are unbearable;
the road to the difficult horse-faced ender is hard, and the state of being a preta is exceedingly terrible.
Having considered this even in the mind, one should turn away from sin.

children.text: smaraṇaṃ kīrtanaṃ viṣṇoḥ sadaiva na parityajet ||
children.translated_text: One should never abandon remembrance and chanting of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
Blessed <s>Vedavyāsa</s>:
Frightened by the utterance of the names <s>Acyuta</s>, <s>Ananta</s>, and <s>Govinda</s>,

children.text: naśyanti sakalā rogāḥ satyaṃ satyaṃ vadāmy aham ||
children.translated_text: all diseases perish. Truly, truly, I say this.

children.text: sakṛd uccāritaṃ yena harir ity akṣaradvayam
children.translated_text: By whomever the two syllables 'Hari' have been uttered even once,

children.text: baddhaḥ parikaras tena mokṣāya gamanaṃ prati ||
children.translated_text: by him the girdle has been fastened for the journey toward liberation.

children.text: evaṃ brahmādayo devā ṛṣayaś ca tapodhanāḥ
children.translated_text: Thus the gods beginning with <s>Brahmā</s>, and the seers rich in austerity,
praise the lord <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the best of gods, the sovereign deity.

children.text: kiṃ tasya dānaiḥ kiṃ tīrthaiḥ kiṃ tapobhiḥ kim adhvaraiḥ
children.translated_text: What need has he of gifts, what of tīrthas, what of austerities, what of sacrifices,

children.text: yo nityaṃ dhyāyate devaṃ nārāyaṇam ananyadhīḥ ||
children.translated_text: who constantly meditates on the god <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> with undivided mind?

children.text: nityotsavo nityatā ca nityaśrīr nityaśo jayaḥ
children.translated_text: There is perpetual festival, perpetual constancy, perpetual splendor, and perpetual victory
for those in whose heart dwells blessed <s>Hari</s>, the abode of auspiciousness.

children.text: jīvaṃś caturdaśād ūrdhvaṃ puruṣo niyamena tu
children.translated_text: A man who lives beyond fourteen, by fixed rule,

children.text: strī vā 'py anūnadaśakaṃ dehaṃ mānuṣam ārjate ||
children.translated_text: or a woman who has reached not less than ten, obtains a human body.
Living beyond fourteen, and saṃsāra being without beginning,

children.text: ato 'vittvā paraṃ devaṃ mokṣāśā kā mahāmune ||
children.translated_text: therefore, without knowing the supreme god, what hope of liberation is there, O great sage?

children.text: ā caturdaśamād varṣāt karmāṇi niyamena tu
children.translated_text: From the fourteenth year onward, by fixed rule,
this person performs actions that are the causes of bodies lower than ten.

children.text: ataḥ karmakṣayān muktiḥ kuta eva bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: Therefore how indeed will liberation arise from the exhaustion of karma?

children.text: samānāṃ viṣamā pūjā viṣamāṇāṃ samā tathā
children.translated_text: Equal worship of unequals, and unequal worship of equals likewise,

children.text: kriyate yena devo 'pi svapadād bhraśyate hi saḥ ||
children.translated_text: when performed by someone, causes even a god to fall from his own station.

children.text: vittaṃ bandhur vayaḥ karma vidyā caiva tu pañcamī
children.translated_text: Wealth, kinship, age, action, and learning as the fifth:

children.text: etāni mānyasthānāni garīyo yad yad uttaram ||
children.translated_text: these are bases of honor, each later one being weightier than the preceding.

children.text: guṇānusāriṇīṃ pūjāṃ samāṃ dṛṣṭiṃ ca yo naraḥ
children.translated_text: The man who performs worship according to qualities, and maintains equal vision
toward all beings, <s>Viṣṇu</s> is pleased with him.
As one should act toward friends, and toward the sons of fathers and enemies,

children.text: tathā karoti pūjādi samabuddhiḥ sa ucyate ||
children.translated_text: so he performs worship and the like; he is called one of equal understanding.

children.text: tiryakpuṇḍraṃ na kurvīta samprāpte maraṇe 'pi ca
children.translated_text: One should not make a horizontal mark, even when death has arrived,

children.text: na cānyan nāma vibrūyāt paraṃ nārāyaṇādṛte ||
children.translated_text: nor should one utter any name other than supreme <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.

children.text: naivedyaśeṣaṃ devasya yo bhunakti dine dine
children.translated_text: One who eats, day after day, the remnant of the deity's offering,
for each morsel there is merit greater than a hundred cāndrāyaṇa vows.
When a straight and gentle ūrdhvapuṇḍra is seen on the forehead,

children.text: sa caṇḍālo 'pi śuddhātmā pūjya eva na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: even if he is a caṇḍāla, he is pure-souled and worthy of worship; there is no doubt.

children.text: aśucir vā 'py anācāro manasā pāpam ācaran
children.translated_text: Whether impure, or even of improper conduct, committing sin in the mind,

children.text: śucir eva bhaven nityam ūrdhvapuṇḍrāṅkito naraḥ ||
children.translated_text: a man marked with ūrdhvapuṇḍra is always pure indeed.
The face of one without ūrdhvapuṇḍra is like a cremation ground.
Having looked at their face, one should look at the sun.

children.text: yajño dānaṃ tapaś caiva svādhyāyaḥ pitṛtarpaṇam
children.translated_text: Sacrifice, gift, austerity, self-study, and offering to the ancestors:

children.text: vyarthaṃ bhavati tat sarvam ūrdhvapuṇḍraṃ vinākṛtam ||
children.translated_text: all that becomes fruitless when done without ūrdhvapuṇḍra.
Whomever a person whose limbs are smeared with gopīcandana sees with his eyes,

children.text: taṃ taṃ śuddhaṃ vijānīyān nātra kāryā vicāraṇā ||
children.translated_text: one should know each of them to be purified; no deliberation is to be made here.
The fathers clap their arms, and the grandfathers dance greatly:
'A Vaiṣṇava has been born in our family; he will carry us across.'
The life of a devotee of <s>Viṣṇu</s> is preferable, even if only five days.

children.text: na tu kalpasahasrais tu bhaktihīnasya keśave ||
children.translated_text: But not even through thousands of kalpas does it arise for one who is without devotion to <s>Keśava</s>.
What is the use of that man merely being born, a burden on the earth and an enemy of food,

children.text: yo jāto nārcayed viṣṇuṃ na smaren nāpi kīrtayet ||
children.translated_text: who, having been born, does not worship <s>Viṣṇu</s>, does not remember him, and does not even praise him?
Whoever gives to twice-born men sandal paste mixed with gopī-candana,

children.text: api sarṣapamātreṇa punāty ā saptamaṃ kulam ||
children.translated_text: even in a quantity the size of a mustard seed, purifies his family down to the seventh generation.
And the knower should perform the actions that are always enjoined,
without desire; he should be constant.
One who knows past and future and is capable of uplifting the three worlds,
even such a person should not abandon śrauta and smārta conduct.
Whatever one does with knowledge, with faith, and with the Upaniṣadic understanding,
that alone becomes more powerful.
Performing actions here alone, one should wish to live a hundred years.

children.text: evaṃ tvayi nānyatheto 'sti na karma lipyate nare ||
children.translated_text: In this way, and not otherwise, there is no other course for you; action does not cling to a man.

children.text: ācāraś caiva sādhūnām ātmanas tuṣṭir eva ca
children.translated_text: The conduct of good people, and also the satisfaction of one's own self,
is dharma prescribed by the Veda; adharma is the opposite of that.

children.text: niṣkāmaṃ jñānapūrvaṃ tu nivṛttam iha cocyate
children.translated_text: What is without desire and preceded by knowledge is here called nivṛtta, withdrawn action.
And one who practices that nivṛtta way attains the eternal <s>Brahman</s>.
